visual_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 1 consistently draws the SAS triangle with the 5 and 7 sides enclosing the 60° angle and highlights the opposite side as √39, while Lesson 2 has variable-label inconsistencies, omits/unclearly places the included angle in key diagrams, and its final diagram appears to mark the unknown distance on the wrong segment.

interactivity.rationale: Lesson 1 includes a well-formed, wired quiz checkpoint with a real question, plausible options, and a marked correct answer after act_formula, while Lesson 2 provides no gate specs or plan at all, so it has no functional interactivity.

narration_quality.rationale: Lesson 1 provides clear, well-paced narration with correctly spoken math and no raw LaTeX defects, while Lesson 2 has no available narration transcript at all, making it impossible to verify any audio quality.

sync.rationale: Lesson 1 at least provides timed visual cues that mostly align with the narrated references, though a few are early or sparse, while Lesson 2 has no available transcript or cues to verify any synchronization at all.

concept_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 1 correctly applies the Law of Cosines with the included 60° angle, clearly explains the side-angle relationship and simplification to c=√39, whereas Lesson 2 has no available transcript or lesson content to verify correctness or pedagogical clarity.

polish.rationale: Lesson 2 is less modern and somewhat sparse, but it maintains clean rendered typography and consistent readable layouts, whereas Lesson 1 has serious polish issues including raw unrendered LaTeX/backslash text, an initially empty formula box, and occasional cramped split-panel clutter.

aggregator.explanation: Lesson 1 is the clear overall winner: five of six dimension agents favored it, all with very high confidence, across the most substantive areas—visual accuracy, interactivity, narration quality, synchronization, and concept accuracy. The agents found Lesson 1 correctly represents the SAS triangle, applies the Law of Cosines accurately, includes functional quiz interactivity, and provides usable narration and timing cues. Lesson 2 only won polish, with lower confidence, due to cleaner typography/layout, but it lacked or failed to provide sufficient content for several core instructional dimensions. The single polish advantage is not enough to overcome Lesson 1's strong, high-confidence wins in the primary learning-quality categories.
